card.name: Permanent harm outcomes in warnings
card.fires_on: Words that finish a phrase about lasting harm, such as "loss" after "permanent vision", "permanent" before paralysis, or "function" after "impairment of brain". It appears in warning text where untreated problems lead to severe outcomes.

modes.label: Permanent loss
modes.description: The noun "loss" ends a phrase about permanent damage to a sense or organ.
modes.example: Untreated acute angle-closure glaucoma can lead to permanent vision<< loss>>. The primary treatment is to discontinue

modes.label: Permanent before damage
modes.description: The word "permanent" (or its ending) appears just before a named serious injury such as paralysis or brain damage.
modes.example: These hematomas may result in long-term or<< permanent>> paralysis. Consider these risks when scheduling patients

modes.label: Brain function impairment
modes.description: A word completing a harm phrase that is followed by "or death".

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words about death, fatal outcomes and danger as what comes next.
card.plain: It marks the point in a warning where the text is about to name a lasting or deadly consequence.
